findings.claim: Outgoing call impact falsely certifies some dynamic dispatch as a completed empty result: an invocation resolved only to an interface method signature is classified as disjoint, so the outgoing producer neither emits an edge nor marks coverage unfinished, allowing callers to trust a false negative.
proof_refs: src/services/relationships.ts:2025-2027 makes every MethodSignature non-canonical; lines 2065-2084 return disjoint when declarations exist but normalize to zero targets, including interface-method calls.
src/services/relationships.ts:1547-1560 marks only unfinished invocations unsafe and ignores disjoint; lines 1981-1984 then upgrade call coverage to completed.
test/impact.test.ts:1958-1993 covers parameter uncertainty and exact disjoint free-function calls but not interface-method outgoing dispatch.
minimal_correction: classify method signatures without one canonical implementation as unfinished for outgoing coverage and add service/MCP regressions for interface-typed method invocation.

findings.claim: The request-wide work budget excludes BFS and required retention/probe operations, so traversal can perform work beyond work.max_items while reporting only producer charges; consumed_items is therefore not an authoritative performance bound.
proof_refs: src/services/impact.ts:617-627 creates the tracker and passes it only to the relationship resolver; lines 628-659 invoke traversal without passing the tracker.
src/services/impact.ts:402-536 performs dequeue, dispatch, probing, classification, and node/edge admission without tracker charges; lines 319-349 sort and filter edges outside the tracker.
src/services/relationships.ts:799-810 and 869-899 perform membership checks, dedupe, retention, and emission without tracker charges.
The R-01 spec at lines 71-79 requires one budget for BFS, producers, and probes; design.md:69-77 explicitly requires these charges.
minimal_correction: thread the same tracker through traversal and candidate retention, charge every specified BFS/probe/filter/retention/emission unit, and add exact-bound exhaustion tests.

findings.claim: Coverage failures are tracked only by relationship kind, so in a both request an unfinished incoming producer also marks an independently completed outgoing entry unfinished, making the per-direction ledger inaccurate and unnecessarily incomplete.
proof_refs: src/services/relationships.ts:1841-1911 installs separate incoming and outgoing producers, but lines 1941-1968 record failures in Set<RelationshipEdgeKind> and discard direction.
src/services/relationships.ts:1981-1984 leaves every coverage entry of that kind unfinished regardless of entry.direction.
minimal_correction: key producer failures by kind and effective direction, then add a both regression where only one direction is unresolved.

findings.claim: Dynamic method dispatch is published as a single exact compiler-authoritative call instead of unfinished: a call through a base-class-typed receiver resolves to the base implementation even when an override is a possible runtime target, so consumers can trust a guessed callee and unsafe call coverage as complete.
proof_refs: src/services/relationships.ts:2065-2081 selects declarations from the invoked symbol and returns exact whenever they collapse to one LocatedSymbol, with no proof that receiver dispatch is final; lines 1981-1988 then upgrade coverage to completed.
An in-memory target-build Base/Child override probe returned caller->Base.m with completed coverage and incomplete=false.
The R-01 spec lines 35-49 and ADR 0007 lines 33-35 require dynamic targets to be unfinished without guessed edges.

minimal_correction: classify potentially polymorphic/interface/union receiver dispatch as unfinished unless compiler evidence proves one final canonical implementation; emit no edge and add outgoing/incoming override and interface MCP regressions.

findings.claim: Incoming call discovery silently drops exact recursive self-calls and still reports completed coverage, so ast_get_impact can return a false complete-empty incoming result while outgoing returns the exact self-edge.
proof_refs: src/services/relationships.ts:1580-1584 returns when caller.node equals target.node without an unfinished marker; lines 1981-1988 upgrade coverage to completed.
An in-memory recursive-function probe returned no incoming edges with completed coverage and incomplete=false while outgoing returned recur->recur.
The R-01 spec lines 35-43 requires exact caller-to-callee free-function edges and defines no recursive-call exclusion.
minimal_correction: retain exact self-call edges in incoming discovery and add registered-MCP recursive free-function and method cases.

findings.claim: The advertised request-wide work budget does not cover BFS or neighbor processing, so work.consumed_items underreports request work and max_items is not the promised aggregate safety bound.
proof_refs: src/services/impact.ts:617-627 passes the tracker only to createCompilerRelationshipResolver; traverseWithNeighborProvider has no tracker parameter.
src/services/impact.ts:402-405 dequeues without a charge, lines 444-473 classify/adopt neighbors using cancellation checkpoints only, and lines 319-349 sort and scan edges without charges.
The R-01 spec lines 71-79 and ADR 0007 require one budget covering BFS, producers, and probes.
minimal_correction: thread the same tracker through traversal and collectNeighbors, charge dequeue/dispatch/bookkeeping/emission, and add exact-bound traversal exhaustion tests.

findings.claim: A limit or unfinished result in one direction contaminates the other direction's coverage during direction=both because unfinished state is tracked only by relationship kind.
proof_refs: src/services/relationships.ts:1941 and 1967 record only producer.kinds in unfinishedKinds; lines 1981-1984 apply it to every direction entry.
An asymmetric max_edges=1 probe marked both incoming and outgoing call entries unfinished although only outgoing hit the limit.
The R-01 spec lines 5-13 defines coverage per kind/effective direction/endpoint class.
minimal_correction: key producer state by kind plus effective direction and add a both-direction asymmetric-limit regression.

ledger.rootDefect: Dynamic method dispatch is certified as exact or disjoint-complete without proving a single non-polymorphic implementation.
ledger.impact: Impact can publish a guessed callee or false complete-empty result for interface/override dispatch, violating compiler-exact fail-closed authority.
ledger.minimalCorrection: Classify interface, override-capable, union, or otherwise polymorphic receiver dispatch as unfinished unless compiler evidence proves one final implementation; emit no guessed edge and add service/MCP interface and override regressions.

ledger.rootDefect: The shared work tracker is confined to relationship producers and omits BFS, probes, retention, dedupe, and emission work.
ledger.impact: Requests can exceed max_items while reporting a lower consumed_items value, so the public request-wide performance bound is non-authoritative.
ledger.minimalCorrection: Thread one tracker through traversal and relationship retention; charge all specified dequeue, dispatch, probe, filtering, dedupe, retention, and emission units; add exact-bound exhaustion regressions.

ledger.rootDefect: Incoming call discovery drops exact recursive self-call edges while reporting completed coverage.
ledger.disposition: Single-judge severe finding; do not auto-fix unless independently corroborated or explicitly decided by the human.

ledger.rootDefect: Unfinished coverage state is keyed only by relationship kind and contaminates the opposite direction in a both request.
